questions.question: Which keyword makes one class inherit from another class?
questions.explanation: A class names its single parent class with extends. The implements keyword is for interfaces.

questions.question: Which relationship does inheritance model?
questions.explanation: A subclass is a kind of its parent, for example a van IS-A vehicle. HAS-A links are modelled with fields.

questions.question: What does this print? class Hub { Hub() { System.out.print("H"); } } class Depot extends Hub { Depot() { System.out.print("D"); } } class Locker extends Depot { Locker() { System.out.print("L"); } } ... new Locker();
questions.explanation: Each constructor calls super() first, so the bodies finish from the top parent down: H, then D, then L.

questions.question: Which of these does a subclass NOT inherit from its parent?
questions.explanation: Constructors are never inherited. A child writes its own and reaches the parent's with super(...).

questions.question: class Van { private int load; } class MiniVan extends Van { void fill() { load = 50; } } Why does this fail to compile?
options: load is private in Van, so MiniVan cannot access it by name
questions.explanation: Private members exist in the object but are hidden from the child. Use protected or a setter method instead.

questions.question: class Truck { Truck(String reg) { } } class Tipper extends Truck { Tipper() { } } Why does Tipper fail to compile?
options: The hidden super() call finds no no-arg constructor in Truck
String parameters are not allowed in constructors
questions.explanation: Tipper() gets an implicit super(), but Truck only has Truck(String). The fix is to call super("some reg") explicitly.

questions.question: What does this print? class Pack { String tag() { return "box"; } } class GiftPack extends Pack { String tag() { return "gift-" + super.tag(); } } ... System.out.println(new GiftPack().tag());
questions.explanation: The override runs and uses super.tag() to add the parent's text, giving gift-box.

questions.question: Why does Java not allow a class to extend two classes?
options: It would use too much memory
To avoid the diamond problem of conflicting parent code
Because the JVM has only one stack
questions.explanation: Two parents with the same method or state would make it unclear which to use, so Java allows one superclass only.

questions.question: What does this print? class Cart { int wheels = 4; } class Trolley extends Cart { } ... Trolley t = new Trolley(); System.out.println(t.wheels + " " + (t instanceof Cart));
questions.explanation: Trolley inherits the field with its initial value 4, and a Trolley IS-A Cart, so instanceof gives true.

questions.question: Which class sits at the top of every Java class hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Every class extends java.lang.Object directly or indirectly, so the constructor chain always ends there.
